Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

approach noun

a way of dealing with something

also method, way, tackle, go about, try another way

classical

Quint. 6 pr. 14: aliqua vīvendī ratiō quaerenda est
Cic. Brut. 253: dē ratiōne Latīnē loquendī

ratiō, ratiōnis f.

noun, third declension

way, method, plan

Often with a gerund in the genitive: the way of doing something.

Other words

  • via, viae f. — way, method

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Ter. And. 670: aliā aggrediēmur viā

    aliā viā aggredī, to try a different approach.

  • aggredior, aggredī, aggressus sum — tackle, set about; approach (a person)

    verb, third conjugation (-iō), deponent · also used · classical · Ter. And. 670: aliā aggrediēmur viā; Cic. Att. 12.33: Damasippum velim aggrediāre (Lewis & Short)

    To go at a task, or to a person with a request; also, to attack.

Examples

  • Dēceptus sum, at nōn dēfatīgātus. … Hāc nōn successit, aliā aggrediēmur viā.

    I’ve been foiled, but I’m not worn out. … That way didn’t work; we’ll try another approach.Ter. And. 669–670

  • sed vīvimus, et aliqua vīvendī ratiō quaerenda est

    but we are alive, and some way of living must be foundQuint. 6 pr. 14

See also approach, process.
